analysis: Reviewed the supplied base-side excerpts (lines 18814-20277) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json, plus the file_changes patch excerpt. The file is a public golden-vector fixture for the prompt contract. Its content is synthetic: a repeated 'Public synthetic cache-parity input' string, a harmony tool-call example, JSON-object and JSON-schema response_format cases, and token ID arrays. The patch excerpt shows head-side changes: an added additional_context {enable_thinking:false} in a provider body, changed prompt_token_count (803->767), changed chain_hash values and a dropped 768-token block boundary. These are fixture regenerations, so token IDs, block hashes and the prompt contract ID change. There is no executable code, no secrets, no authorization or attestation logic, and no endpoint changes. The units I received are base-side text, and the base ranges I could see (18814-20277) do not overlap the listed changed base ranges (3024-54138). The changed hunks are therefore only visible in the truncated patch excerpt, and I could not verify the head-side content. Related threat context is T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and timing oracle) and TB-007. Block-boundary and chain-hash fixtures feed cache keying, so the matching provider and coordinator code must agree on the new contract. In particular, the additional_context field adds a prompt-affecting parameter that must be bound into the prompt_contract_id or cache key so that cache entries are not shared across differing prompt renderings. That binding lives in code outside this batch, so I cannot verify it. The cited changes show no concrete security regression. Integration should confirm that the Swift and Go consumers of this fixture validate the new prompt_contract_id and that the cache key covers additional_context.
